newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodians want to upgrade ties with S. Korea.
newsitem.headline: Cambodians want to upgrade ties with S. Korea.

text.p: Co-Premier Hun Sen and other political leaders want to upgrade diplomatic ties with Seoul in a bid to boost South Korean investor confidence in Cambodia.

"There is a plan that the presidents of 12 political parties would jointly write to the king (Norodom Sihanouk) suggesting that relations between Cambodia and the Republic of Korea be upgraded to ambassador level," Hun Sen said late on Monday.

"We feel upgrading of diplomatic relations...would give more confidence to the South Korean investors," added the second prime minister during a meeting with a small group of foreign journalists at his country residence.

Hun Sen, deputy chief of the Cambodian People's Party, did not identify the other parties but analysts noted that he had signed cooperation with several groups this year, including republican parties.
However, analysts noted Sihanouk, a long time friend to the late North Korean dictator Kim Il-Sung, was opposed to any contact with Seoul and predicted he would oppose upgrading ties.

Cambodia and South Korea reopened low-level diplomatic ties last year after a 21-year hiatus and the country has formed a particularly good relation with Hun Sen, who is said to be suspicious of Pyongyang.
There are more than 12 South Korean companies currently operating in Cambodia. Two-way trade was worth $20 million last year, with Cambodia only accounting for $2 million in exports.
The two nations signed an investment protection and promotion accord earlier this year.

Meanwhile, Hun Sen acknowledged that recent political tensions between himself and First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh had had an adverse effect "on the spirit of the investors and tourists coming to Cambodia."

Foreign business analysts have said many potential new investors have decided to wait until after elections due next year before committing to projects, while some already in the country have slowed down investments.
